- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for consecutive positive sentiment.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.5) — increase forecast by 2–5% for consecutive negative sentiment.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent price drops — cap forecast increases to 3–5% above prior day unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, reduce forecast by 1–2% for each day with sentiment < 0.3 — especially after negative sentiment streaks.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a drop, delay forecast correction — allow 1–2 days for momentum to settle before adjusting downward.
